item_name: DAM4SAM (Videnovic, Lukezic, Kristan, CVPR 2025; arXiv 2411.17576, 2509.13864), DiDi dataset; EdgeDAM (arXiv 2603.05463)
bibliography: [A] Jovana Videnovic*, Alan Lukezic*, Matej Kristan (University of Ljubljana). 'A Distractor-Aware Memory for Visual Object Tracking with SAM2'. CVPR 2025, pp. 24255-24264, DOI 10.1109/CVPR52734.2025.02259 (poster listing cvpr.thecvf.com/virtual/2025/poster/35133; supplement https://openaccess.thecvf.com/content/CVPR2025/supplemental/Videnovic_A_Distractor-Aware_Memory_CVPR_2025_supplemental.pdf). Preprint arXiv 2411.17576 (v2 4 Dec 2024, https://arxiv.org/html/2411.17576v2); in the preprint the tracker is called SAM2.1++, in the CVPR version DAM4SAM (same study, renamed). [B] Jovana Videnovic, Matej Kristan, Alan Lukezic. 'Distractor-Aware Memory-Based Visual Object Tracking'. arXiv 2509.13864 (v1, 17 Sep 2025); extended journal version of [A] (repository README names IJCV 2026); adds integration into EfficientTAM and EdgeTAM. Same research line as [A], not an independent replication. Code (both): https://github.com/jovanavidenovic/DAM4SAM (Apache-2.0; main file dam4sam_tracker.py, branch master; DiDi download at go.vicos.si/didi, not inside the repo). [C] Syed Muhammad Raza, Syed Murtaza Hussain Abidi, Khawar Islam, Muhammad Ibrahim, Ajmal Saeed Mian. 'EdgeDAM: Real-time Object Tracking for Mobile Devices'. arXiv 2603.05463 (v1 5 Mar 2026; v2 11 Apr 2026 is a WITHDRAWAL notice, 1 KB; comment: not accepted at any conference, framework being revised). Code: 'will be released', no repository. Independent group from [A]/[B]; builds on DAM4SAM ideas.
full_text_checked: [A] arXiv v2 HTML full text read (method, Table 1 ablation, Tables 2-6 and 9, appendix 7.1, 7.4, 7.5 summarised). CVPR camera-ready PDF not opened; only the supplement listing and DOI were checked, so CVPR numbers are assumed equal to arXiv v2 [uncertain]. Code: dam4sam_tracker.py read (gating constants, alternative-mask procedure); the SAM2 predictor internals (add_to_drm, RAM storage in sam2/ folder) were NOT read. [B] arXiv abstract page only; full text not read. [C] arXiv v1 HTML read (method, Tables 2-9); v2 is a withdrawal notice; no code exists.
task_and_output: [A]/[B] Single-object visual tracking and video object segmentation: given the target in the first frame (box converted to a mask by SAM2, or a mask), output a per-frame segmentation mask; for box benchmarks the min-max box of the mask is reported; an empty mask means 'target absent' (SAM2 object-presence head). [C] Single-object box tracking on mobile devices: output one bounding box per frame (CSRT propagation + YOLO detection every 3 frames), with a held box during occlusion.
data_and_independent_videos: [A] No training (training-free). Evaluation: DiDi 180 sequences (274,882 frames, ~1.5k frames each), selected from 808 val/test sequences of GOT-10k, LaSOT, UTB180, VOT-ST2020/LT2020, VOT-ST2022/LT2022 (per-source: LaSOT 86, UTB-180 56, VOT2022-ST 20, VOT2022-LT 7, VOT2020-LT 6, GOT-10k 4, VOT2020-ST 1; appendix 7.5). Also VOT2020 (60), VOT2022 (62), VOTS2024, LaSOT test (280), LaSOText (150), GOT-10k test (180). All test sequences are unseen by SAM2's training in the usual sense, but thresholds were set by the authors and DiDi was used both for ablation (Table 1) and for the headline comparison (Table 2) - no separate held-out tuning split. [B] adds benchmarks (13 in total per abstract) [uncertain: list not read]. [C] YOLOv11s fine-tuned on each benchmark's training split; ablations on a custom non-public 35,000-frame horse-rider dataset; evaluation on DiDi, VOT2020, VOT2022, LaSOT, LaSOText, GOT-10k.
target_size_and_input_resolution: [A] Full frame resized to 1024x1024 (input_image_size=1024 in dam4sam_tracker.py), SAM2.1 ViT-L (also T/S/B in appendix 7.1); targets of arbitrary size, no crop. Target size distribution in DiDi not reported. [C] Full-frame YOLO, then ROI crop kappa=2.0 times target during stable tracking; descriptors are HSV histograms and grayscale patches; target sizes not reported. In contrast, our target is about 9x12 lattice steps inside a crop about 2x the target, on 721 grey hexals.
frame_rate_and_camera_motion: [A] Native benchmark frame rates (mostly 25-30 fps video, LaSOT/UTB with moving cameras and distractor-rich scenes); memory updated every 5 frames. Runtime ~11 fps vs 13.3 fps for SAM2.1 on A100. [C] Detection every 3 frames, 17-27 fps reported; 25 fps on iPhone 15 (Pro Max per Sec. 4.1.3).
detector_and_exemplar: [A] No detector; exemplar = initial frame mask (from a box via SAM2). The initial frame is permanently stored in DRM. Distractors are detected implicitly from SAM2's alternative (non-selected) mask hypotheses. [C] Single-class YOLOv11s detector (fine-tuned per benchmark) + CSRT correlation tracker; exemplar = first box; memory entries are HSV/grey descriptors of verified boxes.
trainable_nodes_and_loss: [A]/[B] None trained: the method is a training-free memory-management policy on top of frozen SAM2.1 (or EfficientTAM/EdgeTAM in [B]); thresholds hand-set (delta=5, theta_anc=0.7, theta_IoU=0.8, area +-20% of median of 10). [C] Only the YOLO detector is fine-tuned (standard detection loss); memory/rules hand-designed; 9.4M parameters total reported.
controls_seeds_splits: [A] Matched baseline: same SAM2.1 model with its default memory (update every frame); ablation chain in Table 1 isolates each rule (skip updates when mask empty; update every 5th frame; DRM written only under reliability; DRM written only under distractor trigger; temporal encoding in DRM; RAM-last variant). Model-size control in appendix 7.1 (T/S/B/L, consistent ~6-7% gain). Threshold sensitivity in appendix 7.4 (theta_anc 0.6-0.9, theta_IoU 0.5-0.8 reported stable). No seeds (deterministic inference), no confidence intervals, no per-sequence paired test; tuning and ablation on the same DiDi used for headline results. [C] Component ablation (Table 7) and buffer-size ablation (Table 8) on a private dataset; no seeds, no CI, no write-rule or distractor-buffer-only ablation.
metrics_and_numbers: [A] arXiv v2: DiDi (VOTS protocol, full 180 sequences, ViT-L, single deterministic run) Table 2: Quality/Accuracy/Robustness SAM2.1++ 0.694/0.727/0.944 vs SAM2.1 0.649/0.720/0.887; SAMURAI 0.680; ODTrack 0.608. This resolves the plan's unverified claim: 0.694 vs 0.649 is the authors' own number, DiDi quality, VOTS-style evaluation on all 180 sequences, both trackers run by the authors with ViT-L; no interval. Ablation Table 1 (DiDi quality): SAM2.1 0.649; skip-update-when-absent (PRES) 0.665; plus update every 5th frame 0.667; DRM written only during reliable tracking (DRM1) 0.672; DRM written only on distractor trigger, without reliability gate (DRM2) 0.644 (below baseline); full 0.694; DRM with temporal encoding 0.669; RAM-last variant 0.685. Other: VOT2020 EAO 0.729 vs 0.681 (Table 3); VOT2022 EAO 0.753 vs 0.692 (Table 4); VOTS2024 quality 0.711 vs 0.661 (Table 5); LaSOT AUC 75.1 vs 70.0, LaSOText 60.9 vs 56.9, GOT-10k AO 81.1 vs 80.7 (Table 6); VOT2022-RT EAO 0.635 vs 0.614 (Table 9). Note: some relative-percent claims in the text do not match table differences (e.g. LaSOT '+7.3%'). [B] abstract: +11% when integrated into EfficientTAM, +4% into EdgeTAM; better than SAM2.1 on 13 benchmarks [numbers not checked in full text]. [C] DiDi quality/IoU/robustness 0.926/0.882/0.973 (Table 2), LaSOT AUC 0.895 (Table 5), VOT2020 EAO 0.849 (Table 3); component ablation Table 7: CSRT only IoU 0.612, full 0.930; buffer size Table 8: 10-10 best (IoU 0.991), 15-15 0.870. These numbers are internally inconsistent (0.930 vs 0.991 for the same default) and implausibly far above all published trackers; paper withdrawn.
tested_conditions: [A] Unseen videos: yes (all evaluation sequences, no training). Target absence: yes (long-term VOT-LT/VOTS sequences; empty-mask frames excluded from memory; PRES ablation +0.016). Similar distractors: yes (DiDi built specifically for this; DRM ablation). Occlusion: yes, implicitly (LaSOT/VOT-LT; reported qualitatively as re-detection after occlusion). Night or low light: not reported. Sequential operation on own predictions: yes (online causal tracking, memory written from own masks). [C] Unseen videos: partially (detector fine-tuned on each benchmark's train split; test split unseen). Target absence: not reported as a separate measure. Distractors: yes (DiDi, multi-distractor Table 9). Occlusion: yes (private horse-rider set). Night: not reported. Sequential own predictions: yes.
mechanism_summary: Published mechanism [A]: SAM2's memory (frames whose features are conditioned on the predicted mask, read by cross-attention) is split into two buffers. RAM (3 slots, FIFO, temporal encoding) holds recent target views, written every 5th frame and never when the predicted mask is empty. DRM (initial frame + 3 FIFO anchor slots, no temporal encoding) holds 'anchor' frames written only when BOTH (i) tracking is reliable (SAM2 predicted IoU > 0.8 and mask area within +-20% of the median of the last 10 frames) AND (ii) SAM2's alternative mask hypotheses diverge from the chosen one (box of chosen mask vs box of chosen-plus-largest-alternative-component overlap <= 0.7), i.e. a second plausible object is present. Thus DRM stores correctly-localised target views taken at moments of ambiguity; the distractor is contained as background context in the same frame encoding, not as a separate negative object. Per the author's clarification, the second buffer is not a collection of 'bad objects' but frames useful for resolving ambiguity. Table 1 shows that the distractor trigger without the reliability gate is harmful (0.644 < 0.649), and that the reliability-gated DRM alone gives only part of the gain (0.672). [B] shows the same policy also helps smaller SAM-family backbones. [C] transfers the idea to boxes: RAM admission if IoU with previous estimate >= 0.5 and area deviation <= 0.20 from running median; DRM anchors promoted from RAM; a negative bank of overlapping detections during occlusion penalises similar candidates (gamma=0.25). Proposed modification for us (not published): selective admission of track-history frames as exemplars of the online ridge target model, gated by detector-based reliability and by the presence of a same-class neighbour inside the FlyVis crop.
transfer_limits: (1) Representation: DAM4SAM relies on SAM2 ViT-L features at 1024 px and on mask-conditioned memory encodings read by learned cross-attention; our readout is an online ridge target model on 34 FlyVis cell-type maps over 721 grey hexals; there is no learned memory attention to exploit context frames, so a DRM frame can only enter as additional regression samples (target positive, neighbour region negative) - a different use. (2) Distractor trigger: SAM2's alternative mask hypotheses have no analogue in FlyVis; the bbox analogue is a second same-class YOLO detection inside the crop (environment signal, not FlyVis) - acceptable as a write trigger but it must not be credited to FlyVis. (3) Crop: our crop is about 2x the target, so a neighbour is often only partially visible; DiDi distractors are in full frames. (4) Time: memory written every 5 frames at 25-30 fps; we have 30 Hz with 4 exemplar observations before loss and loss episodes up to ~30 frames; the anchor pool must come from the pre-loss track history, which may be short for young tracks. (5) Absence: DAM4SAM's absence handling is SAM2's presence head (empty mask); our selected interventions are dominated by absent targets (z13_hinge_target_v1: 58 of 84 selected cases target-absent for D_balanced), and DAM4SAM supplies no new refusal mechanism. (6) Our applied output is a centre correction before ByteTrack/MASA matching, not a mask; DiDi quality does not translate to HOTA. (7) EdgeDAM's evidence is unusable (withdrawn, no code, private ablation data).
research_questions_addressed: 5.2 (target model and memory): direct evidence for a write policy - reliability-gated, distractor-triggered anchors, no writes when absent - with ablations on a hard subset; strongest source in the plan for 'what to write and when'. 5.1 (right object and refusal): design analogy only - DAM4SAM does not add a refusal decision, it reduces drift to distractors by memory content; caution that the distractor trigger without reliability gating hurts. 5.3 (core training): not addressed (training-free). 5.4 (association): not addressed (SOT); caution that box-level guards (EdgeDAM IoU/area admission) are environment rules that could act without FlyVis.
candidate_node_change: Node: exemplar/target-model memory of the FlyVis readout (state/exemplar node), not the core. Change: replace 'last 4 observations before loss' with a two-buffer exemplar set: recent buffer (last 4 observations, as now) + anchor buffer of up to 3 pre-loss frames from the track history, admitted only if (a) reliability: the track was matched to a detection with IoU >= 0.8 to its Kalman prediction [threshold to be fixed before the run] and box area within +-20% of the median of the previous 10 matched frames, AND (b) ambiguity: at least one other same-class detection overlaps the FlyVis crop. Anchor frames enter the ridge target model with the target region as positive and the neighbour's region as explicitly labelled negative (the 'distractor-resolving' sample). Controls: (1) same two-buffer rule on R1 (eye-input features of equal dimensionality) - the no-FlyVis control; (2) stock FlyVis C and modernised D with the same rule; (3) random-anchor control: equal number of reliability-gated frames chosen without the ambiguity trigger (separates the selection rule from 'more observations', which already failed in z13_observed_memory_v1); (4) trigger-only control without the reliability gate (DRM2 analogue, expected to be harmful). Minimal check: offline on train26 functional metric already used in z13 cards (useful-centre share and selected-useful count at fixed coverage), reported on all episodes and on a pre-registered hard subset (episodes with >=1 same-class neighbour in the crop at loss). Success rule (pre-set): D_anchor - D_random_anchor >= +2 p.p. with 95% bootstrap lower bound > 0 on the hard subset, AND D_anchor - R1_anchor > 0 with lower bound > 0. Stop conditions: fewer than 20% of loss episodes have any anchor (coverage too low to matter), or the first criterion fails - then record 'this exemplar-selection implementation did not work' and do not proceed to HOTA. Only if passed: dev35 fixed transfer, then the three-way HOTA comparison (stand / rule on R1 / rule on D).
strongest_objection: DAM4SAM's benefit comes through SAM2's learned memory cross-attention over rich RGB ViT-L features at 1024 px, where an anchor frame carries the target and the distractor in a shared high-dimensional context. Our online ridge model on 34 low-resolution motion/brightness maps has no such reader; adding anchor frames is mechanically close to adding more observations or reweighting target vs background, which already failed (z13_observed_memory_v1: C memory - C single -0.127 p.p. [-5.08; 3.45]; z13_balanced_ridge_v1, z13_hinge_target_v1 no gain). Moreover our bottleneck is refusal on absent targets (58/84 selected cases absent), which DAM4SAM does not address. The ambiguity trigger would come from YOLO, i.e. from the environment. All DiDi numbers are single runs without intervals, with tuning and ablation on the same set.
evidence_strength: [A] peer-reviewed (CVPR 2025), code public (Apache-2.0) and gating constants verified in dam4sam_tracker.py; ablations on one dataset without intervals; independent replications not found, but SAMURAI and later SAM2-memory works report comparable SAM2.1 baselines. Overall moderate for 'the write rule matters in SAM2'; weak for transfer to our features. [B] preprint/journal extension by same authors: moderate-weak (not fully read). [C] withdrawn preprint, no code, private ablation data, internally inconsistent and implausible numbers: weak - idea source only.
where_distinction_is_made: [A] Target found vs similar distractor: in the memory content (DRM anchors chosen at moments of ambiguity) plus the frozen SAM2 decoder that selects among multi-mask hypotheses; distractor presence is detected at write time from the divergence of alternative masks, not by a separate classifier. Target outside search area / absent: SAM2's object-presence (occlusion) head produces an empty mask; DAM4SAM only uses this to block memory writes (PRES). Insufficient data: no explicit state. Map maximum vs right object: SAM2 predicted-IoU and presence scores are used as reliability gates for writing, not as an applied refusal; DAM4SAM adds no new decision on whether to output. [C] Separate decision: confidence-driven switching (CSRT PSR < 0.35, normalised jump > 0.30, or >=2 overlapping high-confidence detections) and a negative bank penalty - a rule-based decision layer outside the representation.
feature_dependence: Strong dependence on rich appearance in [A]/[B]: SAM2/EfficientTAM/EdgeTAM image encoders and learned memory attention; the distractor trigger itself depends on SAM2's multi-mask head. [B] shows gains persist on smaller SAM-family backbones (EdgeTAM +4%), but still RGB foundation features. [C] uses compact HSV-histogram and grayscale descriptors, which would be the closest to low-dimensional features, but its evidence is withdrawn/unverifiable. No evidence that the mechanism works with small temporal motion/brightness features like 34 FlyVis cell types on 721 grey columns [uncertain whether any transfer exists].
association_consequence: Not linked to detection matching in [A]/[B] (single-object). In our stack the anchor rule would change only the ridge target model's centre estimate during loss; its effect on association is via the corrected prediction centre entering ByteTrack/MASA costs. An external guard rule (shift limit or cost check rejecting corrections that raise the correct pair's cost above 0.8, as in the R1 case: 79.7 px shift, cost 0.123 -> 1.0, z13_first_divergence_v1) could prevent the same harmful jumps without any memory mechanism; therefore the guard rule must be part of the no-fly control set. EdgeDAM's IoU/area admission and overlapping-detection checks are themselves environment guard rules.
difference_from_tried: Real difference in the write policy: our observed memory (z13_observed_memory_v1) stored separate pre-loss observations without selection by ambiguity; query memory (z13_query_memory_v1) chose among stored models by current response (selected zero memory weight); balanced weights and hinge background loss (z13_balanced_ridge_v1, z13_hinge_target_v1) changed the loss globally, not which frames are training samples. Not tried: (a) admitting frames from the whole pre-loss track history only when a similar neighbour is present and tracking is reliable, (b) labelling the neighbour region of those frames as explicit negative, (c) the DRM1/DRM2 dissociation as controls. Same as tried (no difference): exemplar matching with absent class and negatives (z13 exemplar matching) already used negatives, so 'negatives from neighbours' alone is not new; 'skip updates when absent' is already implicit because our exemplar is frozen at loss. The DAM4SAM idea therefore differs only in the selection rule for which past frames become exemplars.
memory_write_policy: [A] RAM: every 5th frame (code: frame_index - last_added > 5, i.e. effectively >= 6) when the mask is non-empty; DRM: same timing plus reliability (predicted IoU > 0.8, area ratio in [0.8, 1.2] of the median of the last 10 non-zero areas, current frame included in code) AND ambiguity (min box IoU between chosen box and chosen-plus-alternative-component boxes <= 0.7). Initial frame permanently in DRM. Thresholds hard-coded in dam4sam_tracker.py; minor boundary differences from paper (strict vs inclusive). [C] RAM admission: IoU with previous estimate >= 0.50 and area deviation <= 0.20 from running median; DRM anchors promoted from RAM when >=3 of last 5 RAM descriptors have cosine >= 0.85; negative bank of overlapping detections during occlusion.
distractor_representation: [A] Implicit: distractors are present as background context inside anchor frames; no separate distractor track, buffer of distractor objects or negative class. [C] Explicit: a negative bank of overlapping detections with a similarity penalty.
refusal_evidence_horizon: [A] Single frame: SAM2 presence head per frame; memory writes additionally use a 10-frame area median (short accumulation for reliability, not for refusal). [C] Single frame rule-based switching (PSR, jump, overlap).
loss_on_applied_decision: Not applicable for [A]/[B]/[C] (no training of the decision; hand-set rules). The upstream SAM2 was trained on mask segmentation loss, not on the tracker's applied output under the DAM policy.
association_entry_point: Not applicable in the sources (SOT). For our proposal: state update of the lost track's target model -> corrected centre of the prediction -> matching cost (ByteTrack IoU/MASA) for re-association.
no_fly_control_equivalent: (1) The same two-buffer exemplar rule on R1 eye-input features (required). (2) A detector-level guard: reject a re-association when another same-class detection is within the crop and the corrected shift exceeds a limit, or when the correct-pair cost would exceed 0.8 (Kalman/IoU gating). (3) Hybrid-SORT-style weak cues (confidence, height) in the matching cost. (4) EdgeDAM-style IoU/area admission with HSV-histogram descriptors as an appearance-only memory without FlyVis.
hard_subset_evaluation: [A] Yes: DiDi, 180 of 808 sequences selected by a DINOv2 distractor criterion (each pixel scored by average cosine relation of its DINOv2 feature to target features; a frame qualifies if the ratio of outside-target to inside-target pixels whose score passes the inside average is > 0.5; sequence kept if >= 1/3 of frames qualify; exact score direction taken from a summary of the HTML text) - selection independent of tracker outcome. Our analogue should be pre-registered from detector boxes (same-class neighbour inside crop at loss), not from FlyVis or tracker outcomes. [C] evaluates on DiDi too.
temporal_information_availability: Causal: DAM4SAM uses only current and past frames; a frame written to memory at t affects predictions from t+1; no lookahead, no tree/sequence selection over future frames; latency zero frames (about 20% more compute). Our proposal is also causal: anchor frames come from the pre-loss track history and the trigger uses current detector boxes. EdgeDAM's held-box uses optical flow between consecutive frames, also causal.
depth_level: Full analysis (code, ablations, all fields) as set in the item. Verdict for synthesis: the write rule (reliability AND ambiguity, with the DRM2 ablation showing that ambiguity alone hurts) is the only part that is new relative to our tried z13 variants; it is a reasonable backup candidate for the exemplar node, but its support comes from SAM2 RGB features and it does not address refusal on absent targets. EdgeDAM is downgraded to an idea source (withdrawn).
